newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - March 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - March 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Three soccer teams are likely to be dropped from the Ericsson Cup soccer league next season. The Collingwood Warriors, Canberra Cosmos and Gippsland Falcons are unlikely to remain in the competition, with the only new side to be Carlton. Three other applcations by new clubs will be rejected. Page 22.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor has highlighted performances of his opening batting partners and difficult wickets as part of the reason for his poor form this season. In the past eight Test matches, Taylor has an average of only 18.14, and his ru of 18 Test innings without a half-century is the worst since former captain Kim Hughes twelve years ago. Page 22.

The Cronulla Sharks failed in an attempt to cite an Auckland Warriors player over a high tackle that left star halfback Paul Green with severe concussion and 13 stitches in a head wound. As the incident was obscured on video, no further action will be taken. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian cricket team may rest a number of leading players for the one-day series against South Africa. Glenn McGrath, Steve Waugh, Ian Healy and captain Mark Taylor are likely to step down from the side to prepare for the upcoming Ashes series aganst England. Page 46.

The Sydney Swans have rejected a story that they were allowed to escape the repayment of a $A2 million debt, claiming that there was no expectation that the money was to be repaid. The money relates to a rescue package by the AFL when the Swans were in a financial crisis in 1992. Page 46.

Australian Rugby League officials will ask Kerry Packer to delete a clause in the contentious player loyalty agreements. The contracts are being tested in the Industrial Court, with one clause claimed as being particularly unfair and obscure. The hearin resumes on May 19. Page 46.
THE AGE

According to the captain of Australian Football League team Geelong, Barry Stoneham, a win in tonight's Ansett Cup grand final against Carlton would prove vitally important for the success-starved Geelong despite the team's poor recent grand final record. Page 3.

Australian world championship silver medallist cyclist Lucy Tyler-Sharman won the 3000 metres individual pursuit in a time of three minutes 36.423 at the Australian titles last night. Tyler said her good form was due to "80 percent abuse and 20 percent mental effort". Page 12.

Australian Victorian tennis centre Kooyong could also become the home to basketball if the results of a feasability study prove the move to put a dome over the centre court viable. Kooyong general manager David Wilson said the club is keen to maxmise thesite to its best use, so long as the needs of club members are not disrupted. Page 12.
THE HERALD SUN

A $A30,000 cheque presented to Australian world champion skier Kirstie Marshall this week was just a drop in the ocean compared to the millions of corporate dollars going towards the Sydney Olympics - a fact Marshall notes well in her quest for sponsorshi in the lead-up to next year's Winter Olympics in Japan. Page 105.

Australian motorcycle riders will be under pressure to defend a remarkable record at this weekend's opening round of the Superbike World Championship on Phillip Island. Since first hosting a championship round in 1988, an Australian rider has won at leastone of the two races in each round - a record unmatched by any other country. Page 100.

An International Olympic Committee memo recently circulated has stated boxing, weightlifting and wrestling will all reportedly face cutbacks for the 2000 Olympics. The move comes as part of a bid to squeeze in more sports and countries while keeping the total number of athletes below 10,000. Page 105.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Owen Craigie, the Aboriginal Newcastle Knights player who started rugby league's racism controversy, claims he was sticking up for all races when he reported verbal abuse from the weekend's game against Norths. Craigie was satisfied with the action taken and does not regret the affair. Page 126.

A secret dossier prepared by the Queensland cricket team on their opponents for this weekend's Sheffield Shield final, the West Australian team, has been removed from the Queensland rooms and leaked to a local radio station. The Shield final starts today in Perth. Page 124.

The Seven Network has denied rumours that it will cease coverage of the Super 12 series following early poor ratings. Head of network sport Jeff Weil has claimed the story was absolutely untrue. Page 121.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
